subject: Constraining factor loadings to be the same for identification purposes in bifactor model

messages.author: 43d8e5920c5b5dac
messages.subject: Constraining factor loadings to be the same for identification purposes in bifactor model
parts:
Hi Phil,

I am fitting a bifactor model to a 7-item scale. 5 items loads to the 1st specific factor, 2 items load to the 2nd specific factor. To solve the nonidentification due to only 2 items loading to a specific factor, I want to constrain their factor loadings to be the same. The CONSTRAIN keyword in mirt.model does not seem to be used for factor loadings. What should I do? Here is my code:

model <- c(rep(1,5),rep(2,2))
modbifa <- bfactor (data = dataset, model = model, SE.type = "crossprod")

Thank you!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Constraining factor loadings to be the same for identification purposes in bifactor model
parts:
You should constrain the slope parameters to be equal, not the factor loadings. That solves your identification issues. Cheers.

Phil

Thank you for your reply.

I am trying to fix the slopes using the model function, but receive the error: "CONSTRAIN = ... indexed a parameter that was not relevant for item 6". Here is my code:

specific <- c(rep(1,5),rep(2,2))
model <- "CONSTRAIN = (6-7, a3)"

modbifactor <- bfactor (dataset, specific, model)

When I fit the model without "model", it estimates the a3 parameters for items 6 and 7. So I am confused why the error says a3 parameter is not relevant for item 6.

I`d appreciate any help on this.

Thank you!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Constraining factor loadings to be the same for identification purposes in bifactor model
parts:
The documentation for the third argument is this:

model2   a two-tier model specification object defined by mirt.model() or a string to be passed to mirt.model. By default the model will fit a unidimensional model in the second-tier, and therefore be equivalent to the bifactor model

So, by default this is something like model2 = "G=1-7". If you omit this 'G' factor then the general factor is not created, and only the orthogonal specific factors are modeled (which is kind of useless; it makes more sense just to estimate separate unidimensional models if that's the case). You need to keep the G structure in the model, and add your constraints here as well since the specific terms are added automagically. 

specific <- c(rep(1,5),rep(2,2))
model <- "G=1-7

CONSTRAIN = (6-7, a3)"

modbifactor <- bfactor (dataset, specific, model)
